newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA AUTO COMPONENT FIRMS COMPLAIN OF LOW GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: INDIA AUTO COMPONENT FIRMS COMPLAIN OF LOW GROWTH.

text.p: India's automotive component makers have urged the government to kick-start demand to reverse a slowdown in growth rates, the Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA) said on Thursday.

ACMA said in a statement that the industry was "struggling to maintain a growth rate of 2 to 3 percent in sharp contrast to the above 30 percent growth rate it has been enjoying over the last three years."

Senior officials and former presidents of the association at a meeting earlier this week voiced strong concern over a sharp and rapid decline in business volumes in the automotive industry over the past few months, ACMA said.
"The ACMA past presidents called for urgent steps by the government to reflate the economy through increased spending to bolster the money supply," the statement said.
They also sought the government's help to boost exports, it said.
The statement said that growth figures for the first quarter of 1996/97 (April-March) painted a difficult picture.

"The April to June figures show a growth rate of plus three percent for cars, nil for jeeps, minus two for light commercial vehicles, minus one for heavy commercial vehicles, minus 10 for scooters, minus 12 for mopeds, minus one for three-wheelers, and plus 16 for motorcycles," the statement said.
